mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 12 months raises the cost of capital, reducing present value of future corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% and remains there for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when inflation expectations are stable.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong corporate earnings news.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) indicates more workers entering the market without corresponding job growth, which increases competition for jobs and suppresses wage growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable (<0.1pp change) while PAYEMS rises by >0.3% month-over-month for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising faster than GDPC1 quarter-over-quarter) signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of fiscal stimulus.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth outpaces GDPC1 growth for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes in the absence of fiscal stimulus, or the effect is reversed during large-scale government spending programs.
